slides.say: m and n are positive integers, and m plus n is odd. Which of the following is true about the expression m to the power of n, plus n to the power of m, plus nine, plus four n?

So m plus n is odd, and that tells us something. Odd plus odd is even, and even plus even is even. So one of them is even and the other is odd. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, dropping the powers, and then plugging in both cases.
[short pause] Let's start by dropping the powers. Remember, a power doesn't change parity, so in a parity question I may drop it. What's left is m plus n, plus nine, plus four n.
m plus n is odd, it's given. Nine is odd. Four n is even, because of the four. And the evens don't matter, so odd plus odd, even. It's always even, choice number one is our answer.
at: m plus n is odd, it
choice number one is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now let's try plugging in. There are only two cases, m odd and n even, or the other way round. m is one and n is two. One squared is one, and two to the power of one is two. One plus two plus nine plus eight is twenty, even.
at: m is one and n is two

slides.say: Now swapped, m is two and n is one. Two to the power of one is two, and one squared is one. Two plus one plus nine plus four is sixteen, even again. Both cases are even, so it's always even. Choice number one. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
